data_source: FRESH re-fetch: N=75 newly downloaded ABIDE CC200 subjects from public fcp-indi S3 (independent sample from the committed N=248 run, same pipeline/split-half design). fetched 100 files in 24.3s

a_mcnemar.basis: fresh N=75, real per-subject correct/incorrect pairs

c_rmt_null.mp_theoretical_bulk_edge_note: MP bulk-edge lambda+ (informational, N=75 subjects, D=19900 edges, q=N/D=0.0038) = 1.1266; with N<<D the relevant comparison is the empirical random-Gaussian-matrix null above, not the asymptotic MP edge, since MP theory assumes fixed aspect ratio with both dimensions large.
c_rmt_null.interpretation: real top eigenvalue far exceeds the random-matrix null distribution

d_node_strength_regression.interpretation: identification survives regressing out each subject's mean node strength (a motion/global-SNR proxy) -> not purely riding on a gross scalar confound

single_session_caveat: ABIDE is single-session per subject (one resting-state scan, split first-half/second-half here). This within-session confound (stable head-motion tendency, global SNR, scanner/site signature shared by both halves of the SAME scan) is NOT fixable with ABIDE data -- there is no independent second acquisition to separate 'trait connectivity' from 'trait scanner/motion signature'. The node-strength regression above (test d) removes the specific GROSS SCALAR version of this confound but cannot rule out subtler within-scan nuisance structure.
between_session_design_needed: HCP test-retest: fingerprint session 1 vs an independently acquired session 2 (different day) per subject, after regressing each session's own mean framewise-displacement and global signal out of that session's edges BEFORE computing the fingerprint. If identification still holds session-to-session after this regression, the within-session confound is ruled out. wiring-not-weights/exp05_hcp_wiring_vs_weights.py already targets exactly this design; it is blocked on HCP's gated Aspera-only data access, not on method design.
